title: Smoky hake and new potato stew

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain staple; the tinned tomatoes and vegetable stock are explicitly allowed.

supermarket.reason: Hake fillets, new potatoes and purple sprouting broccoli are all everyday Tesco lines in April at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: One lidded casserole and simple simmering are well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 750g potatoes, a tin of tomatoes and 500ml stock simmered for 15 minutes, then the fish and broccoli steamed on top for 6 to 8 minutes, gives a properly cooked, well-seasoned stew for four.

honest_times.reason: Slicing an onion and garlic, halving the potatoes and trimming the broccoli fits 15 minutes, and the steps add up to about 28 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including parsley and lemon, is used in the steps under its true name, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: New potatoes are the bulk of the stew and lead the title, and a light fish stew suits a cool April evening.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no fuss or jargon.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fish, potatoes, tomatoes and greens make a balanced, satisfying family dinner.
